newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnians, NATO soldiers celebrate Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Bosnians, NATO soldiers celebrate Christmas.

text.p: Hundreds of Sarajevo residents celebrated Christmas Day at midnight masses and soldiers in the NATO-led peace force attended separate services at their military camps in the Bosnian capital.
The city's Roman Catholic cathedral was crowded as the country marked its second peaceful Christmas since the end of the Bosnian war in November 1995.

A smaller mass was held in the district of Stup which was badly damaged in the war. Those attending had to dress warmly because of the freezing winter weather as the church's roof was destroyed during the Serb siege of Sarajevo.
NATO organised Protestant and Roman Catholic services and masses in English, French and German for troops stationed in Sarajevo, said alliance spokesman Major Jan Joosten.
Senior officers were due to serve up a traditional Turkey dinner for soldiers in the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) later on Christmas Day.
U.S. General William Crouch, commander of the SFOR mission, planned to visit the main American base in the northeastern town of Tuzla, where about 3,000 soldiers are stationed.
Some 8,000 U.S. troops are serving in the 35,000-strong multinational force which has been given 18 months to enforce the Dayton peace agreement.
